item.title: Activation‐Induced Turbostratic Ordering in pDCPD‐Derived Hard Carbon Enables Stable Carbonate‐Based Sodium‐Ion Storage
item.description:

Advanced Science | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in using poly(dicyclopentadiene)-derived hard carbon with activation-induced turbostratic ordering, where activation effects depend on carbonization temperature. This yields enhanced rate performance and 88.1% retention after 500 cycles in carbonate electrolyte (352 mAh at 0.1 C). Significance: a cost-effective route to high-performance, long-cycle-life sodium-ion battery anodes.

item.title: Unlocking electric vehicle flexibility in microgrids via lightweight on-charger coordination
item.description:

Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in transforming resource-constrained on-board chargers into intelligent agents via a lightweight distributed coordination framework, cutting memory use by 96.1% and communication overhead by 74.3%. Its significance: unlocking hardware-level vehicle flexibility yields a 10.8% profit gain over uncoordinated charging and promises economic, environmental, and social benefits for the 2025–2040 energy landscape.

item.title: Nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage lithium batteries via preemptive passivation
item.description:
الکترولیت غیرقابل اشتعال سولفامویل-کربنات با غیرفعال‌سازی پیشگیرانه دو الکترود، پایداری چرخه در ولتاژ بالا و تأخیر ۸۷ درجه‌ای در runaway گرمایی را فراهم می‌کند.
Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte that forms a weakly solvating environment, enabling preferential preemptive passivation of both electrodes. Its significance is achieving ~0 s self-extinguishing time, stable high-voltage cycling in lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries, improved rate and low-temperature performance, and an 87 °C delayed thermal runaway onset—offering a viable route to safe, high-energy batteries.
